title: Transformation and Orchestration Services: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Transformation and Orchestration Services: Visual Guide

1. From Load To Transform | the five-stage platform strip — ingest, store, transform, integrate, serve — with the orchestration band spanning it, each stage tappable to show its service and the lesson that taught it | Dataform, Cloud Data Fusion and the orchestrators occupy different LAYERS from the ingestion and BigQuery services already covered, and most wrong answers are a correct service from the wrong layer

2. The Dependency Graph | the doc's worked example (cleaned_orders, cleaned_customers, customer_segments, daily_sales, a revenue assertion) scheduled three ways — hand-written list, compiled graph, and graph with one false dependency — on a minute-by-minute timeline | ref both qualifies the name and declares the edge, so the compiled graph runs independent branches together (10 min instead of 15) and a dependency that is not real costs you the branch (12 min)

3. Compile Then Execute | two phase boxes plus five tappable defects — a bad ref, an IAM denial, a missed late-arriving event, a failed assertion, a wrong production schema — each lighting up the phase it lands in | compilation is hermetic and deterministic and never touches BigQuery, so triage starts by naming the phase, and the incremental-predicate defect is the dangerous one because nothing fails

4. Fusion Run Modes | the same four-node logical pipeline held constant while the compute profile switches between preview on a subset, an ephemeral Managed Spark cluster, and an existing Spark environment, with the still-yours risk chips below | design and execution are separate concerns in Cloud Data Fusion, preview proves the design and never production volume or permissions, and managed removes cluster babysitting rather than engineering responsibility

5. Airflow Or Workflows | six requirement toggles that tip a balance bar and write a defensible selection statement naming the capability and the accepted operational burden | the orchestrator choice follows operating model rather than Python versus YAML, so hundreds of scheduled DAGs and backfills point at Managed Airflow while an event-driven chain of managed API calls points at Workflows
